How long do they have to register them?","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"answer":{"text":"Thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"rationale":{"text":"New residents have thirty days to register their vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Paperwork for your vehicle","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"The title.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Registering and renewing.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Addresses and plates.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the section on vehicle services and maintenance. This first lesson covers the paperwork that goes with owning a vehicle in Washington. We start with the Certificate of Ownership, usually called the title, then move to registration: who must register, when, and what you need to bring. After that we cover the yearly registration you receive with your tabs, the separate address record for your vehicle, and the rules for displaying license plates. Each rule is simple on its own, but several have deadlines worth memorizing.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The Certificate of Ownership","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"DOL issues a title for most vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Shows owners, VIN and any lender.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Keep it safe, never in the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"DOL issues a Certificate of Ownership, called the title, for most vehicles. The title shows the registered and legal owners, the Vehicle Identification Number, or VIN, and any lender. Because it proves ownership, the guide says it should be kept somewhere safe but never in the vehicle. So the glove box is exactly the wrong place for it. Keep the title at home or another secure spot, and keep a different document, the yearly registration, in the vehicle instead. To remember: dOL issues a title for most vehicles; shows owners, VIN and any lender; keep it safe, never in the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who registers, and when","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Every vehicle must be registered.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},{"text":"New residents: thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},{"text":"Bought out of state: right away.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every vehicle must be registered with DOL. You need a driver license to register one, unless the law exempts you, in which case you file a Vehicle Registration Driver License Exemption form. The timing depends on your situation. New residents have thirty days to register their vehicles. A vehicle bought in another state should be registered in Washington right away. So a newcomer gets a short window, while an out-of-state purchase should be registered immediately. To remember: every vehicle must be registered; new residents: thirty days; bought out of state: right away.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What registration needs","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"The current title, or a replacement.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"A Washington license for every owner.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Yearly registration: sign it, keep it inside.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To register a vehicle you need its current title. If it is lost, you get a replacement from the issuing state. You also need a Washington driver license for every registered owner, not just one of them. After that, registration repeats each year. You receive a new registration each year when you renew your tabs, and you must sign it and keep it in the vehicle. So the title stays safely at home, while the signed registration rides with the car. To remember: the current title, or a replacement; a Washington license for every owner; yearly registration: sign it, keep it inside.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"One address, two records","fact_ids":["sec03-R07","sec03-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: license address updates the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec03-R07","sec03-F06"]},{"text":"The vehicle address is separate.","fact_ids":["sec03-R07","sec03-F06"]},{"text":"Update it online or at an office.","fact_ids":["sec03-R07","sec03-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Many people update the address on their driver license and assume the vehicle record follows. It does not. Updating the address on your driver license does not update your vehicle address. You change the vehicle address separately, online in License Express or at a vehicle licensing office. Changing your driver license address leaves the vehicle address unchanged, so the two records must each be updated. After a move, plan on two updates, one for the license and one for the vehicle. To remember: the vehicle address is separate; update it online or at an office.","fact_ids":["sec03-R07","sec03-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Displaying your plates","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Front and rear plates.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Clean and readable.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Frames must not cover letters, numbers, tabs.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"License plates have display rules. Plates must be displayed clean and readable on both the front and the rear of a Washington-registered vehicle. A plate frame is allowed, but only if it leaves the letters, numbers and tabs uncovered. So a decorative frame is fine as long as nothing on the plate is hidden. A frame that covers the tabs, or a cover that obscures the characters, does not meet the rule. Both plates, front and back, need to stay clean enough to read. To remember: front and rear plates; clean and readable; frames must not cover letters, numbers, tabs.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check: new residents","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A family moves to Washington.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},{"text":"Two cars to register.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},{"text":"How long do they have?","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a family has just moved to Washington with two cars registered in their old state. How long do they have to register the cars here? Decide before the answer. They are new residents, not people buying a car out of state. The answer is thirty days. New residents have thirty days to register their vehicles. If they had instead bought a vehicle in another state after living here, it should be registered in Washington right away. Either way, every registered owner also needs a Washington driver license to register.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Registration recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Title safe, never in the car.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Register; newcomers within thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Two address records; clean plates.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, DOL issues a title showing the owners, the VIN and any lender, and you keep it somewhere safe but never in the vehicle. Every vehicle must be registered, with an exemption form for owners the law exempts from holding a license. New residents register within thirty days; an out-of-state purchase is registered right away. Bring the title and a Washington license for every owner, sign the yearly registration and keep it in the car, update the vehicle address separately, and keep both plates clean and readable.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u02","module_id":"sec03-m02","objective_ids":["sec03-u02"],"title":{"text":"Selling a vehicle","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The seller files a Vehicle Report of Sale within five days and removes the plates.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07"]},{"text":"The report of sale does not transfer ownership; We will start with the seller's report of sale and license plates, then the buyer's title transfer, and finish with what changes when a dealership is involved. The two deadlines in this lesson are easy to swap, so pay close attention to which person each one belongs to. To remember: the seller's duties; the buyer's duties; dealer sales. To remember: file a Vehicle Report of Sale; within five days; take the plates off.
